ownership_reason: Only the gold decides the kind of each attribute of a list of two or more slots: it adds the attribute held in each slot, in slot order. Hops 1, 3 and 4 only wrap, create and pass the list; hop 2's shortcuts apply to no slot and to a single slot only, so the three-slot list of the trigger is built entirely by the gold. Once the gold has added a plain Attribute for the valueless 'boolean' slot, a BooleanAttribute can appear at index 1 only if a caller rewrites the gold's output or replaces the gold. In jsoup's attribute model the attribute held in a valueless slot is a boolean attribute (Attributes tracks boolean attributes as null values; BooleanAttribute is the attribute written without any value), so the variant breaks the gold's contract on the trigger input. The convention is pinned outside the gold: Attribute.isBooleanAttribute() (a null value makes a boolean attribute), Attribute.shouldCollapseAttribute (a null value always collapses) and Attributes.html (a null-valued slot is written as its key alone), and hop 2's single-slot shortcut makes the same decision; ElementTest::testAddBooleanAttribute (through the chain: a single null-valued slot is listed as a BooleanAttribute), ElementTest::booleanAttributeOutput, SelectorTest::testByAttributeStarting (through the gold) and TokeniserTest::handleSuperLargeAttributeName pass.
